definition: after 'that' as the subject, use a full verb with -s, not an -ing form
example: I want an app that keeps me learning every day.
exampleEs: Quiero una app que me mantenga aprendiendo todos los días.
cloze: I want an app that ____ me learning every day.
note: You said 'an app that keeping me learning'. After 'that', use a full verb: an app that keeps me learning.

definition: made from or built using something as the starting point
example: The plan is based on this paragraph.
exampleEs: El plan está basado en este párrafo.
cloze: The plan is based ____ this paragraph.
note: You said 'based in this paragraph'. 'Based in' is only for places (a company based in Mexico); for ideas and sources it is 'based on'.

definition: want + person + to + verb; Spanish 'quiero que' never becomes 'want that' or 'make you to'
example: I want you to connect the app with Tivra.
exampleEs: Quiero que conectes la app con Tivra.
cloze: I want ____ connect the app with Tivra.
note: You said 'I want to make you to connect'. Use want + person + to + verb: I want you to connect it.

definition: to give an instruction, use the base form of the verb, not the past
example: Please make a script that checks the logs.
exampleEs: Por favor haz un script que revise los logs.
cloze: Please ____ a script that checks the logs.
note: You said 'made a script' as an instruction. Instructions use the base form: make, write, send.

definition: to act dishonestly to win or pass; 'cheater' is the person, 'cheat' is the action
example: I tend to cheat a lot when a test is hard.
exampleEs: Tiendo a hacer mucha trampa cuando un examen es difícil.
cloze: I tend to ____ a lot when a test is hard.
note: You said 'I tend to be like very cheater'. 'Cheater' is a noun (I'm a big cheater); for the action use the verb: I cheat a lot.

definition: to watch and check something over a period of time
example: The app will monitor my progress every week.
exampleEs: La app va a monitorear mi progreso cada semana.
cloze: The app will ____ my progress every week.
note: 'Monitorize' is not an English word (it comes from Spanish 'monitorizar'). The verb is simply monitor.

example: AI is the most valuable skill in the industry right now.
exampleEs: La IA es la habilidad más valiosa de la industria en este momento.
cloze: AI is the most valuable skill in the industry ____.
note: You said 'in this time'. For the present, say right now, at the moment or these days.

definition: a judgment of how good or what level something is
example: I need an evaluation of my English level.
exampleEs: Necesito una evaluación de mi nivel de inglés.
cloze: I need an evaluation ____ my English level.
note: You said 'an evaluation that of my English level'. Plan the phrase before you start: an evaluation of + the thing.

definition: to ask or talk about meaning, use 'what ... means'
example: I don't know what the word means.
exampleEs: No sé qué significa la palabra.
cloze: I don't know ____ the word means.
note: You said 'which kind of word I have'. To talk about meaning: what does it mean? / I don't know what it means.

definition: very much; one strong adverb sounds better than repeating 'very'
example: The game has extremely high engagement.
exampleEs: El juego tiene un engagement extremadamente alto.
note: You said 'very, very, very good levels of engagement'. One strong word is more natural: extremely high, really strong.

definition: the present perfect describes a recent change that still matters now
example: Since I joined the new team, I have started having meetings in English.
exampleEs: Desde que entré al nuevo equipo, he empezado a tener reuniones en inglés.
cloze: Since I joined the new team, I ____ having meetings in English.
note: You said 'I start getting some meetings in English'. For a recent change, use the present perfect: I've started having meetings.

definition: after 'that', the verb agrees with the noun before it; plural noun, plural verb
example: I like applications that have a clear goal.
exampleEs: Me gustan las aplicaciones que tienen un objetivo claro.
cloze: I like applications that ____ a clear goal.
note: You said 'applications that has'. The verb agrees with the plural noun: applications that have.
